headline: Corn sits at $4.36½ after Wednesday's 2.5% drop; export sales due
lead: Corn gave back 11¼ cents Wednesday and wheat gave back 25¼, the worst day for both in weeks.
teaser: Corn sits at $4.36½ after Wednesday's 2.5% drop; export sales due.

one_number.unit: Gulf corn export bid, barge CIF
one_number.context: That is the basis USDA AMS reported for corn at Gulf export elevators on Nov. 18, against 95 to 105 over January for soybeans.

sections.title: Grains edge up after drop
sections.body:
- Dec corn is at **$4.36½** overnight, up a penny from Wednesday's settle, after two straight lower closes.
- Jan soybeans are at $12.22¾, up 6 cents, after lower closes, and Dec wheat is at $5.78¼.

sections.title: Hogs lag, cattle firm
sections.body:
- Dec lean hogs settled Wednesday at **$51.35**, down 3.3%, while the Dec live cattle settle was $219.775, up 0.5%.
- USDA AMS put cash hogs at $38.75 carcass base on 3,049 head, and the pork cutout at $69.48.

outside_the_pit.title: Thailand trade deal includes $2.6 billion in US ag purchases
outside_the_pit.body: Thailand would also open its market to US pork, which would add a buyer for hog producers.

outside_the_pit.title: Screwworm cases rise sharply in Texas, New Mexico and Arizona
outside_the_pit.body: A faster spread raises the odds of tighter cattle movement rules in the Southwest.

outside_the_pit.title: Boozman says a farm bill can pass this year
outside_the_pit.body: The Senate Ag chairman said staff on both sides can reach compromises, a sign of progress on farm programs.

outside_the_pit.title: Cal-Maine bird flu case hits 1.4M hens in Florida
outside_the_pit.body: About 2.7% of the company's flock will be depopulated, which can tighten egg supplies.

source_summary: CME Group futures, USDA AMS, USDA calendar, AGSIST news digest

facts.sentence: Basis firmed this week: Ohio soybeans +5¢ (37 of 62 bids moved), Ohio corn +5¢ (42 of 55) and Indiana soybeans +5¢ (31 of 46).
facts.detail: Each state's middle change in a week, across bids matched with the same elevator's same delivery and futures month; states with 30 or more such bids from 8 or more companies.

theme.headline: December corn fell 11¼ cents Wednesday to $4.35½
lead: December corn settled down 11¼ cents Wednesday at $4.35½, a 2.5% drop.
That is the lowest of the 35 settles on file since Oct. 1.
